description: L1ght's open-source tools: GPU monitoring and sharing, remote development and coding-agent tools, desktop apps, LaTeX helpers, frontend templates, and hardware hacks such as a NAS-hosted phone line.
lead: Each one started as a fix for a real problem: shared GPU servers, coding agents, papers and odd hardware. Every tool here is released, with a way to install or open it. Research prototypes stay off this page.

sections.title: GPU & compute
sections.intro: Tools that came out of running shared GPU servers: see what is busy, split a card fairly, and develop CUDA code on a machine with no GPU at all.

projects.pitch: See the GPUs on all your SSH servers in one terminal view, and queue jobs onto whichever has room.
Run CUDA-facing code and plan GPU memory without a real GPU: fake devices for PyTorch, NVML and NCCL calls, plus memory estimators for LLM training and serving.
Split one NVIDIA GPU's SMs and memory between jobs, give one of them priority, and rebalance while they run.
An nvtop-style terminal monitor for the GPU and Neural Engine on Apple Silicon Macs.

sections.title: Remote dev & agents
sections.intro: For working on remote machines and alongside coding agents: providers, skills, shells and files, without setting up the server first.

projects.pitch: A desktop panel for switching Claude Code providers on remote SSH servers, compatible with cc-switch.

install.label: Download for macOS, Windows or Linux

projects.pitch: Keep the skills of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and other coding agents in one store, and switch whole skill sets at once.
Turn a shell you already have (tmux, a web terminal, docker exec, ssh -T) into file and command tools for an agent, with an MCP server.
Mount a remote code-server workspace as a local folder over NFS or WebDAV, with only its URL and password: no SSH needed.
Run Linux VMs on a Mac with different CPU, memory, network and browser setups, and audit the device details each guest can see.

sections.title: Network & cloud
sections.intro: Desktop apps that replace hand-edited config files and clunky web consoles.

projects.pitch: Edit Surge profiles with structured editors, a live preview of the .conf and a tester that shows which rule a URL matches.

install.label: See it on the showcase site

projects.pitch: A desktop browser for Alibaba Cloud OSS: tabs, an editable oss:// address bar, previews and an upload/download queue.

sections.title: Papers & LaTeX
sections.intro: Reading other people's LaTeX, and writing your own outside the browser tab.

projects.name: XTX (arXivTeXplorer)
projects.pitch: A Chrome extension that opens any arXiv paper's TeX source in a VS Code-style viewer, with a file tree and highlighting.
Mount Overleaf projects as a local folder and edit them in any editor, or with Claude Code; changes sync back on save.

sections.title: Web templates
sections.intro: Frontend starting points pulled out of real projects: copy one folder, swap in your own content, and it builds and deploys on its own.

projects.pitch: Copy-ready Vite + React templates for an annotation console, a slide deck, a product page and a progress report, all on one toolchain with light and dark themes. Try each one with sample data in the live gallery.

sections.title: Hardware
sections.intro: Getting unusual hardware to talk to a Mac or a NAS.

projects.name: CBD (CellBridge-Docker)
projects.pitch: Turn the first-generation DJI 4G module and a SIM card into a second line for your iPhone: a Docker gateway on your NAS carries VoLTE calls and SMS over Tailscale, and YakPhone rings even when the phone is locked.
Use the first-generation DJI 4G dongle as a USB modem on macOS, with an AT console, SMS and eSIM tools.

projects.name: MTM (Mifare Tool)
projects.pitch: A macOS app for reading and writing Mifare Classic cards with a PN532 NFC module.

sections.title: Campus life
sections.intro: Small fixes for university systems: subject registration, VPNs that drop, and waiting for results.

projects.pitch: A Chrome extension that makes PolyU subject registration searchable, with timetables, vacancies and clash checks inline.
The PolyU GlobalProtect VPN in a Docker container, with a web panel for the MFA login and a local SOCKS5 proxy.

install.cmd: git clone https://github.com/FanBB2333/PolyGP.git && cd PolyGP && cp .env.example .env && docker compose up -d --build

projects.pitch: A desktop app that watches ZJU thesis blind-review results and sends a Bark notification when they change.
A watchdog that signs a dropped aTrust VPN session back in, by looking at the remote desktop over SSH and VNC.

sections.title: Agent skills
sections.intro: Skills that change how a coding agent reasons or writes. They work with Claude Code, Codex and other agents that read SKILL.md files.
sections.after_html: To use one, copy its folder into your agent's skills directory, for example .claude/skills/<name>/ for Claude Code.

projects.name: HundredSchools
projects.pitch: Fourteen schools of philosophy, from Daoism to Popper, turned into planning and checking strategies, with a guide for picking one per task.
The model grills its own draft for gaps and jargon first, then explains the answer from first principles.
Debug in four diagnostic phases, borrowed from traditional Chinese medicine, before writing a minimal fix with a test.

projects.name: Humandex
projects.pitch: Strips corporate jargon, filler openers and flattery from GPT models' Chinese output.

projects.name: GPTify
projects.pitch: The opposite direction: gives Claude, Gemini and other models GPT's chatty Chinese style.

projects.name: SIGMEOW
projects.pitch: A joke skill: a cat walks across the keyboard and leaves harmless mischief in the agent's code.
